data.description:
## Report

The Gerrit LLM-Review bot does not reliably queue a review when a patch set is uploaded. The change sits with `LLM-Review = --` indefinitely, and only starts reviewing after a human/agent posts a `recheck-review` comment.

## Evidence — two independent observations, 2026-08-07

1. **Change 1486 (ticket 599e):** the agent reported the bot "silently skipped BOTH uploads and needed a `recheck-review` comment to queue". Two patch sets, neither auto-reviewed.
2. **Change 1490 (ticket e7a9):** no vote after upload. The agent posted `recheck-review` at 11:41; the bot voted `LLM-Review -1` at **11:44** — 3 minutes later. So the bot was healthy and fast ONCE TRIGGERED; it simply never queued on the upload.
3. **Fleet-level corroboration:** a Gerrit query of all open changes at ~11:50 showed `LLM-Review = --` on 1486, 1488, 1491, 1492, 1493, 1494 and 1495 simultaneously, with the most recent vote anywhere being 1477 at 11:28. Verified votes were landing normally on several of those in the same window, so CI was queueing and the reviewer was not.

## Why this is worse than a delay

It is INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM AN OUTAGE, and it caused a real misdiagnosis: the e7a9 agent concluded "the reviewer looks down rather than backlogged" and STOPPED work on a completed, correct change. The change had in fact been reviewed and rejected on two legitimate findings minutes earlier. An agent cannot tell 'not yet queued' from 'bot is down' from 'reviewed, still thinking', because all three present as `--`.

Second-order cost: every change needs a human to notice and nudge it, which silently serialises the whole review pipeline on operator attention. During this session that was the binding constraint on landing work, alongside GitHub Actions capacity.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Root cause established for why the upload event does not queue a review (webhook not delivered? delivered and dropped? queued and lost? a filter rejecting the event?) — proven, not inferred
- [ ] A patch-set upload queues a review WITHOUT any manual comment, proven by an end-to-end test that uploads a patch set and asserts a vote lands
- [ ] If the trigger can still fail, the failure is OBSERVABLE — a change that has been waiting on an un-queued review beyond a bounded time is surfaced, rather than being indistinguishable from a pending review
- [ ] `recheck-review` remains available as a manual override, but is no longer the routine path
- [ ] The distinction between 'not queued', 'queued and running', and 'reviewed' is visible to an agent or human inspecting the change, so the e7a9 misdiagnosis cannot recur
data.title: LLM-Review bot silently skips new patch-set uploads; a change stalls unvoted until someone manually posts recheck-review
